name: Huygens–Coster pendulum clock
description: A pendulum regulated a spring-driven clock with a verge escapement; Huygens developed the arrangement and Coster made early clocks at The Hague.

date.label: December 1656
date.basis: Museum retrospective attributes a successful Huygens pendulum clock to December 1656.

events.statement: The Science Museum dates a successful Huygens pendulum clock to December 1656.

evidence.supports: Reports December 1656 and the spring-driven verge arrangement.

contributions.resource: Pendulum regulation of a spring-driven verge clock.

evidence.supports: Attributes the 1656 pendulum clock to Huygens.

date.basis: The Metropolitan Museum dates exclusive Dutch patent rights to 1657.

events.statement: Coster obtained exclusive rights to make Huygens’ pendulum clocks in the Netherlands.

evidence.supports: Identifies Coster, 1657 and the territorial scope of the rights.

contributions.resource: Exclusive rights in the Netherlands to make Huygens pendulum clocks.

evidence.supports: Reports Coster held the exclusive Dutch rights.

date.basis: Museum catalogue date range for the surviving clock, not a universal production interval.

events.statement: The surviving Science Museum clock 1980-108 is catalogued as made by Coster at The Hague in 1657–1659.

evidence.supports: Identifies the maker, location and date range of the surviving object.

events.caveats: Catalogue date of a single surviving object; no production volume or date of invention is established.

date.label: By November 1658
date.basis: The Metropolitan Museum states that the London advertisement was in place by November 1658.

events.statement: After John Fromanteel worked as a journeyman with Coster, the Fromanteels advertised pendulum clocks in London by November 1658.

evidence.supports: Reports the workshop connection and London advertising.

events.caveats: The report of an advertisement does not establish a sale, price, production volume or the precise date the journeyman work began.

earliest_record.rationale: Museum-reported earliest scoped working clock here; no general first-for-all-clockwork claim.

caveats: This records the Huygens–Coster pendulum clock rather than all earlier mechanical clocks; exact origin and earlier influences remain open.

missing_prerequisites: Spring-driven clockwork with a verge escapement used as the inherited mechanical arrangement.

unresolved.note: The museum describes a conventional spring-driven verge clock adapted to pendulum control; the exact earlier design and any specific source record still need research.

evidence.supports: Describes a conventional spring-driven verge clock adapted for pendulum control.

research.note: Independent parent checked the SMG catalogue and Met essay: working design, territorial rights, surviving object and London offer remain separate.

witnesses.limitation: This object attests manufacture in 1657–1659; it does not itself date the December 1656 design.
